record.title: Google announces Gemini 4 Carbon with vendor-reported cybersecurity and long-horizon results
record.summary: Google announced Gemini 4 Carbon on Oct 28, 2026, with initial access for a subset of cyber defenders and broader access described as forthcoming. Google reports strong cybersecurity and agentic benchmark results and internal improvements in secure-code generation and alignment-related measures. At review time, Artificial Analysis lists Carbon at Intelligence Index 59 and the CWE-bench owner lists it at 71% deterministic pass@1 and 81% pass@4 over 120 private held-out tasks. Those leaderboard entries provide third-party benchmark-owner reporting, but this review did not inspect raw outputs or rerun either evaluation; SEC-bench Pro did not list Carbon and the linked ExploitGym repository was inaccessible. The announcement lists introductory API prices, but current public pricing docs did not show a Carbon SKU and no API access or billing was verified.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: Google announced Gemini 4 Carbon on Oct 28, 2026, saying initial access would go to a subset of cyber defenders and broader developer, business and consumer access would follow later. The announcement lists introductory API prices of $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens, with $4 and $20 prices after the introductory period. The current Gemini API pricing page lists those dated prices for Argon but did not show a Carbon SKU during this review; Carbon access and billing were not verified.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Google reports that Gemini 4 Carbon scored 59 on Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5.0, 88.2% on SEC-bench Pro, 54.8% on ExploitGym and 71.0% on CWE-bench. At this review, Artificial Analysis independently lists Carbon (high) at Index score 59, and CWE-bench lists 71% deterministic pass@1 and 81% pass@4 (71%/83% on its three-judge panel). SEC-bench Pro’s visible leaderboard does not list Carbon; ExploitGym’s linked repository was inaccessible in this review. No raw Carbon outputs were audited or benchmarks rerun.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Google reports internal improvements over Argon in secure-code generation and alignment-related measures, including more than 2x uplift on an internal secure-code benchmark, nearly 80% fewer high-severity monitoring alerts in internal live coding, about 2x fewer unsupported claims, and 26% lower overreach with 29% lower under-service. These remain Google-reported internal measurements, not independently validated here.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The reviewed sources establish public leaderboard entries for Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index and CWE-bench, but do not establish raw outputs, full evaluation reproducibility, matched conditions across all claimed benchmarks, broader customer outcomes, deployment safety or general reliability. SEC-bench Pro does not currently list Carbon; ExploitGym protocol access failed.

evidence_gaps.description: No independent raw-output audit or the research desk rerun of the reported Artificial Analysis, CWE-bench, SEC-bench Pro or ExploitGym evaluations was conducted.
The announcement does not provide enough detail to align benchmark conditions or estimate customer-facing reliability, safety and cost.
The CWE-bench owner does not post Carbon cost per rollout, and Artificial Analysis task cost uses weighted benchmark token usage rather than realized end-user cost.

Google’s public Gemini API pricing page did not show a Carbon SKU, and the model-specific documentation route was not accessible in this check. Announced rollout and rates therefore do not establish operational API access or billing terms.

brief.importance_rationale: If Google’s reported cybersecurity and sustained coding capabilities hold under independent, matched evaluation, they could materially change frontier model selection, cyber-defense workflows and agent deployment risk. This score reflects consequence if true; results remain vendor-reported and initial access is restricted.
limitations: All model performance and safety metrics in the announcement are company-reported; they were not independently reproduced in this review.
Benchmark-specific protocols, inference settings, tool access, guardrails and scoring conditions were not established across the cited results.
Initial access is restricted to selected cyber defenders; broad developer, business and consumer availability is not yet established by this announcement.
Posted introductory prices do not establish realized cost, latency, reliability or comparative economic value.
CWE-bench is a benchmark-owner leaderboard with a private held-out task set; the research desk did not inspect raw Carbon runs, and Carbon cost is not posted.
Artificial Analysis reports an independent index score, but per-task Carbon outputs and the complete evaluation trace were not inspected in this review.
The SEC-bench Pro leaderboard page did not list Carbon during this check, so it does not corroborate Google’s reported 88.2% result.
ExploitGym repository retrieval failed; its protocol and Google-reported 54.8% result remain unassessed here.
Google’s current API pricing documentation lists the dated Argon prices but did not show a Carbon SKU in this review; announced Carbon rates and restricted rollout were not verified through API use.
brief.summary: Google announced Gemini 4 Carbon on Oct 28, 2026, with initial access for a subset of cyber defenders and broader access described as forthcoming. Google reports strong cybersecurity and agentic benchmark results and internal improvements in secure-code generation and alignment-related measures. At review time, Artificial Analysis lists Carbon at Intelligence Index 59 and the CWE-bench owner lists it at 71% deterministic pass@1 and 81% pass@4 over 120 private held-out tasks. Those leaderboard entries provide third-party benchmark-owner reporting, but this review did not inspect raw outputs or rerun either evaluation; SEC-bench Pro did not list Carbon and the linked ExploitGym repository was inaccessible. The announcement lists introductory API prices, but current public pricing docs did not show a Carbon SKU and no API access or billing was verified.

technical.claimed_result: Google reports high scores on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, SEC-bench Pro, ExploitGym and CWE-bench, plus internal security, alignment and long-horizon coding outcomes. These remain attributed company claims.
technical.demonstrated_result: The dated first-party announcement establishes that Google announced Gemini 4 Carbon on Oct 28, 2026, described restricted initial defender access and listed introductory API prices. It does not independently demonstrate the reported performance outcomes.
technical.mechanism: Google identifies Carbon as a model in the Gemini 4 family built for sustained agentic coding and cybersecurity work. The announcement describes availability via a limited defender cohort and reports model benchmark and internal evaluation outcomes; the training or serving mechanism is not specified in the reviewed source.
technical.regime: Google’s Oct 28 announcement and public benchmark-owner pages current at review time. CWE-bench uses 120 held-out private tasks, high reasoning, four rollouts per task, a one-hour limit, deterministic exploit/regression verification and a separate three-judge panel; its cost estimate for Carbon is absent. Artificial Analysis publishes its Index score but this review did not inspect per-task raw outputs. SEC-bench Pro reports a separate 344-instance fixed-budget leaderboard where Carbon was not listed.
technical.strongest_baseline: CWE-bench lists Carbon at 71% deterministic pass@1 versus Gemini 4 Argon 68% under its high-reasoning Antigravity condition; Carbon’s cost is not reported, while Argon is listed at $6.63 per rollout. The public methodology specifies four one-hour rollouts per each of 120 held-out tasks; the task set is private. This is a benchmark-owner comparison, not a matched evaluation independently rerun by the research desk. SEC-bench Pro’s visible leaderboard does not list Carbon.

brief.title: Google announces Gemini 4 Carbon with vendor-reported cybersecurity and long-horizon results
brief.why_it_matters: A model that combines long-running coding capability with strong vulnerability discovery, validation and repair could affect cyber-defense workflows and frontier-model evaluation. The announcement makes the result worth tracking, while its vendor-reported metrics, restricted initial access and lack of independent reproduction limit what can be concluded about actual capability or deployment impact.
